solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Accommodated as royal, delicate fabric placed in room

indicators.note: to be placed in something is to be put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a pad is informal for a flat or room
lace is a fine openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A royal guest's room has been fitted out with fine fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A pad is informal for one's room or flat; PALACED is a rare word, but it simply means lodged in a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: To be palaced is to be housed in a palace, which is how monarchs are lodged.

clue.text: Fairy Liquid initially taken from bottle

indicators.note: what comes initially is at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
something taken from a whole is removed, so the larger word loses a letter

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for courage, as is pluck
the first letter of this word is removed

explanation.surface: It reads like a cheeky ad for Fairy Liquid washing-up soap poured from its bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairy Liquid is a British brand of washing-up liquid, so the two words seem to belong together; 'Fairy' alone is the definition. PLUCK minus L gives PUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck is the mischievous sprite in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, an example of the folklore type.

clue.text: Hero’s beloved name appearing in editorial

indicators.note: to appear in something is to show up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a newspaper's leader is its editorial column
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial reveals the name of a hero's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' looks like any brave man, but it is Hero of Greek myth, a priestess. N goes inside LEADER.
explanation.definitionFit: In the myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his lover Hero, the priestess at Sestos.

clue.text: Supreme commander involving gunners in good time

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: CIC stands for commander-in-chief
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British gunners

explanation.surface: A top general brings his artillery along to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supreme commander' is the commander-in-chief, abbreviated as three letters; the gunners are the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Craic is Irish slang for fun, lively conversation and enjoyable company.

clue.text: European Union with drive set up exchange

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
drive and go both mean travel or run
set down, as a table is set or laid

explanation.surface: The EU sets up a trade exchange with real drive behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: EU, GO and LAID are put together and the whole is turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialogue is a conversation, an exchange of words or views between parties.

clue.text: Plant shown in Ask the Family persistently?

blocks.note: to pump someone is to ask them persistently, the last word of the clue completing this sense
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A plant appeared on the old quiz show Ask the Family, it seems, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Ask the Family was a long-running British TV quiz. Read it as an instruction: ask persistently is PUMP, and the family is KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is a trailing gourd plant grown for its large orange fruit.

clue.text: Calm provided with fleet offering defence?

indicators.note: a defence is a wall put round something to protect it, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: fleet means fast, as does pacy
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Peace is kept by a navy whose fleet stands guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a navy, but it is the adjective meaning swift; IF is wrapped in PACY.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe or quieten someone, bringing them to a calm state.

clue.text: Animal god happy with miracle periodically

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: Mars is the Roman god of war
feeling up means cheerful
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A beast that is divine, joyful and miraculous now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: From miracle take letters two, four and six to finish MARS UP IAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsupial, such as a kangaroo, is a mammal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Wonk finally given time can nail constituent

indicators.note: what comes finally comes at the end, so only the last letter of the word is used

blocks.note: its last letter
an era is a period of time
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A policy nerd, given time, can nail down a key component of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can nail' reads as verb and verb; really 'can' is TIN and 'nail' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratin is the fibrous protein that makes up fingernails, hair and horn.

clue.text: Judah’s son up and back in extremely short period

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Onan was a son of Judah in Genesis
to back a proposal is to second it

explanation.surface: A biblical son gets up and comes back in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: ONAN reversed gives NANO, then 'back' as a verb means support, which is SECOND.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is one billionth of a second, a vanishingly brief instant of time.

clue.text: Outside a bar cleaner caught early bus

indicators.note: what is outside surrounds, so one set of letters wraps round another

blocks.note: a char is a cleaning lady
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A cleaner, waiting outside a pub, caught the first bus of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR and C together go outside A BAN. 'Bar' suggests a pub and 'early bus' the first service, but here early means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an open-topped motor coach used for outings in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Sappers collapse denied one later showing

indicators.note: what is denied is withheld, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
a collapse is a ruin
I is the Roman numeral for one, removed here

explanation.surface: Army engineers' collapse is shown again on TV later.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are the Royal Engineers, a standard crossword abbreviation; 'one' is the Roman numeral that goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a repeat broadcast of a programme already aired once before.

clue.text: Play from Spike, productive American inspiring us

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is drawn inside another

blocks.note: to spike a drink is to doctor it
fat land is fertile and productive
taken as written
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A play by Spike, perhaps Spike Lee, a productive American film-maker who inspires us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a name such as Spike Lee, but it is a verb. FAT US takes in US to give FAUSTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Faustus is Christopher Marlowe's Elizabethan tragedy about a scholar who sells his soul to the devil.

clue.text: Each tale revised to feature home and housekeeper

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Every story, once edited, gives a role to the home and the woman who runs it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' is the common crossword sense of being in, and it joins the other letters before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the woman in charge of a large house and its domestic management.

clue.text: Hurried through Dutch city avoiding the belligerent speech

indicators.note: to avoid something is to leave it out, so a word is dropped from the name
going through something means passing inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: ran means hurried
The Hague, with its article dropped

explanation.surface: Someone rushed through a Dutch city making an aggressive speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's name includes its article, and 'avoiding the' strips exactly that word before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, forceful, aggressive address or lecture to an audience.

clue.text: Celebrity with false teeth and plaque

blocks.note: a big name is a celebrity
a dental plate holds false teeth

explanation.surface: A star with dentures and dental plaque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plaque' looks dental beside 'teeth', but it is a wall sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a small plaque on a door or desk showing who works or lives there.

clue.text: Piece of cake — choose to cut both ends off

indicators.note: with both ends off, each of the two words loses its tail

blocks.note: to choose is to pick
a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: Instructions for slicing a cake: pick a slice and trim both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both ends' looks like the two ends of one word; it means the end of each word, so PICK and NICK each lose their K.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is no picnic means it is hard, so a picnic is an easy task, idiomatically.

clue.text: Swimmer good leading another two?

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
two more swimmers: ray and ling are both fish

explanation.surface: A strong swimmer heads a relay team of two more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another two' means two further swimmers, and both are fish: RAY and LING.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Streetcar crossing close to you a shock

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken
to cross something is to straddle it, so one piece spans the other

blocks.note: a streetcar is the American term for a tram
its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tram crossing right in front of you gives you a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes into TRAM, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a deeply distressing experience, a severe emotional or physical shock.

clue.text: Contract that could make ferry operator redundant?

definitions.text: that could make ferry operator redundant?

blocks.note: first meaning: shorten, as a book is cut down

blocks.clueFragment: that could make ferry operator redundant?
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two words: a crossing built over the water that puts boats out of business

explanation.surface: A business deal that could put a ferry company out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun for a deal, but it is the verb. Split the answer as A BRIDGE for the cryptic half, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, making it contract; a new bridge would end any need for a ferry.

clue.text: Great number into working on both sides of trench

indicators.note: letters that are working are in action and moving about, so they are rearranged
a piece placed on both sides of another flanks it, so it wraps around

blocks.note: taken as written
a rill is a small channel or trench

explanation.surface: Lots of people are busy working on both sides of a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a preposition but is the anagram fodder, split in two to flank the small stream that serves as the trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A trillion is a million million, a huge number in modern usage.

clue.text: Chinook’s mid-section catches branch left hanging

indicators.note: the mid-section is the middle part, so only the central letters are kept
to catch something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: the middle three of its seven letters
a limb is a branch of a tree

explanation.surface: A Chinook helicopter's middle snags on a branch and is left dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chinook is a big twin-rotor military helicopter; its middle three letters split round the branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in limbo is to be stuck in uncertainty, awaiting a decision, as when a matter is left unresolved.

clue.text: Nasty gremlin runs out to fraternise

indicators.note: when something runs out it leaves, so a letter is removed
something nasty is twisted and ugly, so the letters are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, removed here

explanation.surface: A nasty little gremlin rushes out to socialise.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop R from GREMLIN and rearrange the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle is to circulate and chat sociably at a gathering, much as to fraternise is.

clue.text: Senior cabinet minister provides rally in reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle mixes things into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior minister organises a political rally during a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: A reshuffle is when the British prime minister moves ministers between jobs, so the indicator fits the cabinet surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Privy Seal is one of the great officers of state in the UK, usually sitting in cabinet.

clue.text: Worry about class with fool lacking distinction

indicators.note: what is lacking is missing, so some letters are removed
about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to eat someone is to bother them, as in what's eating you
taken as written
an ass is a fool, removed here

explanation.surface: Fretting about a class whose clown has no flair.
explanation.walkthrough: Worry is the sense in 'what's eating you?'; the fool leaves the class, and what remains sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant success or showy flair, the kind of acclaim that marks someone out.

clue.text: Let it be said that Euterpe turned heads

indicators.note: heads are tops or fronts, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of each of four words

explanation.surface: The rumour goes that the Muse Euterpe looked round.
explanation.walkthrough: Euterpe was the Greek Muse of music, a decoy name; only the initials matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's mark meaning leave the text as it was, ignoring a correction.

clue.text: Home help in retreat finds country I may represent

indicators.note: something in retreat moves back the way it came, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
aid is help

explanation.surface: A home help on a retreat discovers a country she might stand for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home help' looks like a single phrase for a carer, but splits into IN and AID; I stands for this word in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter I is spoken as India, so I represents that country.

clue.text: Bird takes fruit endlessly — there’s remorse about that

indicators.note: without an end, a word loses its final letter
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: guilt is remorse
a citrus fruit, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A bird steals fruit without stopping, then feels sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like it describes the taking, but it trims the citrus fruit before guilt wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family that nests on cliffs.

clue.text: Lover who was for one summer in France an interpreter

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
e.g. means for example, for one
été is French for summer

explanation.surface: A former boyfriend spent one summer in France working as a translator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover who was' is a roundabout way to say a former lover.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete is someone who expounds and explains texts, especially scripture, which is a kind of interpreting.

clue.text: Take a hike? Let’s go rambling around Thailand’s capital

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, the one that starts a word, so only the first is kept
to go around something is to enclose it, so one piece sits inside
rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so these letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
its capital, meaning first letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to go walking around Bangkok, Thailand's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thailand's capital' wants to be Bangkok; it is just the capital letter T. 'Take a hike' is slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are rude idioms telling someone to go away and leave you alone.
